purpose: Test whether pinned BackdoorBench feature detectors, especially SCAn, are applicable when the victim task has eight classes.

attack.selection: uniform without replacement from all non-target training indices
attack.construction: replace selected training images in place, overwrite their labels with target class, and preserve original sample indices

victim.normalization: channel mean/std computed once from the clean official training split
victim.paired_training: clean and suspect models use identical initialization and shuffled-index order for a seed
victim.checkpoint_policy: save clean and suspect best-epoch state dictionaries, normalization values, seed, protocol hash and SHA-256 for every attempted development seed

evaluation.clean_metric: balanced accuracy on the untouched official test split
evaluation.attack_metric: target-class attack success rate on patched official non-target test images

detector_pool.trusted_reference: all clean official validation samples with true labels
detector_pool.candidates: the full in-place poisoned official training set with assigned training labels

backdoorbench_spectre_oracle_target.contamination: 600 for class 6 and zero for every other class

backdoorbench_spectre_uniform_5pct.contamination: floor(0.05 * candidate count) independently in every assigned class

development.expansion_gate: both victims eligible; all eight classes present with at least two trusted samples; SCAn scores finite and class-score range greater than 1e-8 in both views; sample mappings and confusion counts replay; at least one seed is within runtime budget

confirmation.ten_seed_expansion: only after at least four of five confirmation victims are eligible and runtime remains practical

interpretation.negative_result_policy: retain and report victim or detector applicability failure without retuning on confirmation seeds
interpretation.scope: P6-A upstream-baseline applicability; CF-CMD comparison is a later frozen add-on after this gate
